title: Simplify the Tags workbench policy editor and insights layout
description:
Problem: the live `/tags` review showed multiple nested scroll regions and dense policy textareas above a separate insights tab/table area. Policy editing, feedback, usage, and suggestions are all visible at once, which makes the route feel crowded and reduces the visible area for both editing and analysis. A continued visual-density pass also measured roughly 41 inputs, 20 combobox-like controls, repeated namespace removal actions, and a long insights table, reinforcing that the route needs stronger workflow separation.

Desired outcome: Tags should separate policy editing from insights cleanly while preserving fast access to both workflows.

Scope:
- In scope: clearer edit/insights modes or collapsible policy sections, better save-state visibility, textarea sizing, tag table density, suggestion review density, and responsive behavior for Usage/Suggestions tabs.
- Out of scope: changing tag policy file format or validation rules.

Acceptance criteria:
- Policy editing gets enough vertical room to edit allowlist/blocklist/aliases without fighting nested scrollbars.
- Insights tables remain scannable and do not compete with open textareas unless the user chooses a split view.
- Suggestions can be reviewed efficiently without a very long table dominating the route.
- Dirty/saved policy state is clear without requiring permanently large command buttons.
- The layout preserves fast refresh/save actions and keyboard navigation.

Validation:
- Capture `/tags` screenshots in edit-heavy, usage-insights, and suggestions-review states.
- Run focused checks for policy edit, save, tab switching, suggestion approve/reject affordances, and no horizontal overflow.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created from 2026-05-25 live visual review: `/tags` shows policy controls, large textareas, feedback, and insights at once, producing nested-scroll density and weak workflow separation.
